title: Orchestrated dual-region traffic drain and session-resilient failover for hosted API
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Problem: Active-active hosted API gateways must fail over traffic between regions without dropping in-flight streaming sessions or breaking session affinity. Current blunt-region-switch approach causes reconnect storms, lost KV cache warmup, and SLO degradation for streaming and low-latency clients.

Goal: Implement an orchestrated 'traffic drain + dual-controller' pattern that shifts new request allocation, gracefully migrates in-flight streams when possible, preserves conversational prefix cache where appropriate, and applies tiered load-shedding and circuit-breakers to protect global SLOs. The solution must be observable, reversible, and compatible with existing runtime fallbacks.
acceptance_criteria: New region steering API allows operator to start traffic drain with parameterized windows (0-300s)
In-flight streaming sessions that opt-in to handshake can be migrated without message loss >= 95% of sampled sessions
KV cache warmup transfer reduces cold-token ratio on target region by >= 40% within first 2 minutes of drain for pinned models
No regression in host-level 99th percentile latency for non-streamed requests during a controlled failover (<= +10% relative)
Circuit-breaker triggers and load-shedding policies engage automatically under overload and produce graceful 503/429 behavior documented in API contract
Playbook produced and validated in canary with runbook steps for abort/rollback and emergency manual drain completion
design_notes: Dual-controller model: a coordinator in control-plane issues per-region drain tokens; edge gateways subscribe to tokens and apply local transition logic (drain, redirect, cutover)

Traffic drain semantics: differentiate new HTTP requests (route away immediately) vs streaming sessions (attempt soft-handshake migrate; if migration fails after timeout, continue draining existing connection until completion or enforce hard cutover)
Session affinity: use sticky session tokens with explicit origin-region metadata so clients and SDKs can retry intelligently; avoid transparent reassigns that break streaming protocols
KV cache propagation: best-effort prefix push for hot conversational contexts using encrypted delta blobs in control plane; older prefixes evicted by LRU if memory pressure
Backpressure-aware router: when target region is under heavy load, apply incremental percentage-based steering rather than binary cut to avoid overload amplification
SLO alignment: steering and load-shedding thresholds are calculated to keep global error budget burn within safe bounds during failovers
rollout_plan: 1) Feature flag gating and internal-only rollout to 'staging' region pair
2) Dry-run mode: emit telemetry about drift without enforcing routing changes for 48h
3) Canary: enable steering for <1% production traffic on non-critical customer segments
4) Progressive ramp: 1% -> 5% -> 25% -> 100% over multiple maintenance windows with monitoring gates
5) Post-rollout: 72h elevated monitoring and automated rollback if SLO thresholds breached
telemetry_and_slos: Primary SLOs: regional request P99 latency, global streaming continuity rate, error-rate (4xx/5xx) and tail token generation latency
New metrics: drain_start_ts, drain_phase, migrated_session_count, migration_success_rate, kv_prefix_sync_latency, kv_warm_ratio, steering_rate_by_region
Alerting: create composite alert when migration_success_rate < 90% AND global error-rate increases > 0.5% over baseline
Dashboards: per-region heatmap showing steering percentages vs. available capacity and per-model warm/cold token ratios
circuit_breaker_policy: Three-tier CB per region: (1) soft window - increased retry backoff, (2) hard window - reject new requests above safety throttle, (3) emergency - divert all eligible traffic to fallback model tier
State transitions keyed by weighted error signal (5min EWMA) and CPU/GPU utilization thresholds
CB preserves streaming sessions where possible, but will reject new stream initiation requests when in hard/higher state
Operator tools to force-open/close CB for maintenance with audit log entries
load_shedding_strategy: Prefer prioritization over blind shedding: mark best-effort routes and non-critical customers for early shed
Token-based shedding: per-customer token quotas reduce allowance proportionally under load
Graceful HTTP responses with structured body describing retry-after and fallback recommendations
Rate-capacity curve stored in config service; steering respects capacity headroom when shifting traffic
Automatic shed amplification limited to X% per minute to avoid cascade failures
streaming_session_considerations: Handshake protocol: optional 'resume' capability where client sends stream-id + last-ack offset; server attempts to rehydrate KV cache and continue generation context-aware if model variant compatible
If resume not supported, apply slow-drain: allow existing streaming connection to finish with lower priority scheduling but refuse new streams
Keepalive and ping frequency adjustments during drain to detect stale clients and free resources
Edge proxy respects ordered delivery; re-ordering within migration window disallowed to prevent conversation corruption
Client SDK updates required: expose explicit retry behavior and region hint headers; older SDKs fall back to reconnect semantics documented in migration playbook
test_plan: Unit tests for drain token lifecycle and per-edge transition guards
Integration tests: simulate region failover with mix of short API calls and long-lived streaming sessions; assert migration success metrics
Chaos tests: provoke partial KV sync failures and validate rollback of steer decisions and bounded error budgets
Load tests: synthetic traffic shaped by real customer distributions to verify steering ramp safely under high QPS
DR drill runbook with SREs to practice manual abort and emergency cutover scenarios
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: migration handshake increases per-request latency for participating sessions -> Mitigation: make handshake opt-in and apply to <10% of sessions during canary
Risk: KV prefix sync may expose customer data if misconfigured -> Mitigation: encrypt blobs with customer KMS keys and restrict transfer to control-plane authenticated channels
Risk: cascading redirects could overload receiving region -> Mitigation: implement backpressure feedback loop and reject redirects when capacity falls below safety floor
Risk: older SDKs mis-handle region hints leading to reconnect storms -> Mitigation: detect and bucket old SDK traffic and exclude from early canaries; include SDK compatibility header in telemetry
notes: Aligned with platform thesis: serving stability and predictable inference is core differentiator
Coordinate with runtime team for model-variant fallback compatibility and quantization considerations
Schedule post-mortem template for any unplanned failover within 30 days
Follow-up work: automate KV prefix pre-warm for popular conversational flows (separate ticket)
